absent: Locking, serialization, and concurrency rules for nested cache, secondary control structure, and vCPU state.
Full layouts, widths, and numeric values of control and save areas, intercept words, exit codes, and control bits.
Implementation of nested paging setup, paging root load, permission table merge, virtualized interrupt update, Hyper-V identity update, and offset helpers.
Hardware semantics of bus lock counter, pause filtering, prediction tagging, branch record virtualization, virtual NMI, virtual GIF, and next pointer beyond gating shown.
Tracing formats, performance counter effects, and userspace exit payload details.
System management interrupt interception predicate and secure mode interaction beyond the checks shown.

findings.text: VMRUN emulation entry for SVM nesting. Given a vCPU context, it validates host nesting state and the guest supplied control area address, caches that area, retires the trapping instruction, preserves selected L1 processor state, and either enters L2 guest mode or synthesizes a nested error exit. Instruction retirement accounting occurs on paths where the trapping instruction was accepted.

L2 entry transition given a validated control area address and a flag distinguishing architected VMRUN from other entry causes. It records the address for later exit handling, moves execution to the secondary control structure after copying shared state, prepares control and save portions, establishes the paging root, enables global interrupt handling, emits entry tracing, and requests deferred work for nested paging state, virtualized interrupt handling, and Hyper-V identity.

Bus lock throttling state across nested entry follows instruction pointer stability. When the incoming pointer is nonzero and equals the previously recorded value, the throttling indicator stays asserted; otherwise it is cleared. This retains suppression for the same faulting instruction while allowing forward progress to reset the condition.

Nested timestamp translation composes L1 and L2 views. The active offset derives from L1 offset, L2 offset, and current scaling configuration. Effective scaling keeps the L1 factor unchanged when the L2 factor equals the system default; otherwise it is the fixed point product of both factors shifted by a capability defined fractional width. Hardware ratio state is refreshed when rate scaling is guest visible and the current ratio differs from default.

Secondary control initialization resets translation cache control to inert, initializes nested memory context only when nested paging is active while carrying over memory encryption tag enablement from cached L1 intent, merges the interrupt control word from L1 and L2 sources through complementary selections, and copies vector, state, and event injection fields directly from L2 intent.

Next instruction pointer adoption depends on capability exposure and first entry status. When next pointer support is guest visible or entry is not the initial pending dispatch, secondary next pointer and software interrupt resume pointer come from L2 intent; otherwise current execution position is used later. Event injection carrying nonmaskable or software interrupt intent is latched into per vCPU flags for later delivery.

Optional throttling and prediction controls are capability gated. Pause filter count and threshold copy from L2 intent only when the matching features are exposed, otherwise they are cleared. Larger prediction allowance inherits from L2 intent only when the extension is exposed, while the prediction clear request is always asserted on nested entry so the host can emulate host versus guest tagging. Virtualized load save acceleration is enabled when intercept analysis shows it is safe.

Architected VMRUN follows ordered validation before any mode change. Missing save pointer, secure mode execution, failed assist verification, uninitialized nesting state, or invalid control area address each abort with architected fault injection. Control area mapping failure transfers to generic failure handling. After caching, the trapping instruction is retired; if validation already prepared an error exit, handling stops there. On success, L1 state is preserved in the inactive area, a pending run marker is set, and failure of mode entry or permission merge unwinds injection flags and synthesizes an error exit.

Caching of the L1 supplied control area maps the guest page containing the given address, duplicates control and save portions into per vCPU cache, and validates the cached image. Validation failure records an error exit with cleared auxiliary and injection fields in the guest visible area, disables global interrupt delivery, and reports invalid argument, distinct from mapping failure which reports a fault.

Skipping an emulated instruction bypasses pointer update for encrypted guests with hidden state, otherwise prefers hardware provided next pointer when that feature is active and nonzero, falls back to generic emulation when no next pointer exists, optionally preserves flags when side effects are suppressed, and clears interrupt shadow when side effects are committed. Shadow update clears or sets a mask in current interrupt state based on whether the requested mask is zero.

Memory failure during nested control area caching is terminal for the attempt. Propagated fault intent with valid exception detail becomes an emulated page fault injection; any other failure, including input output needed during instruction emulation, becomes a generic emulation failure exit to userspace. Callers must not transparently retry the entry.

Processor state duplication is split into two groups. The run group carries four general segment selectors, descriptor tables, flags with fixed bits forced, extended feature enable, three control registers, two general registers, instruction pointer, and privilege forced to zero, plus conditional shadow stack and branch record state with reserved debug bits cleared when host extensions allow. The load save group carries remaining segments, task and local descriptor selectors, kernel base, system call configuration, and system enter configuration.

Triple fault while nested forwards to L1 only when L1 requested shutdown interception; otherwise it is ignored. Forwarding clears the pending triple fault request and produces a simple nested exit with shutdown indication and cleared auxiliary fields.

Model specific register and port exit ownership follows L1 permission bitmaps. Register evaluation requires global register protection interception, then decodes target register, access direction, and bit position; unrepresentable targets and unreadable bitmap bytes resolve to L1 ownership, otherwise the addressed bit decides. Port evaluation requires global port interception, decodes port number and access width, reads one or two bitmap bytes covering the access, and tests the covered bits.

Exit routing separates host handled from L1 handled outcomes. Run failures always go to L1. Register and port exits delegate to bitmap evaluation, the host intercepted exception range always goes to L1 with injection performed elsewhere, and all other codes consult the L1 intercept bitmap. A decision for L1 immediately synthesizes a nested exit. Separately, nesting instructions require paging plus hypervisor enablement and zero privilege, else undefined opcode or protection faults are queued without mode change.

Exception forwarding is controlled per vector by the cached exception bitmap. Injection forms an exit code from an exception base plus vector, copies error code when present, and treats auxiliary data specially: page fault carries address from payload or fault register, debug delivers pending payload and clears general detect with register synchronization, and other vectors require absence of payload.

Pending nested events are examined in fixed priority: initialization, previously staged nested exception, newly pending exception, system management interrupt where supported, nonmaskable interrupt, and regular interrupt. A pending nested run blocks staged exception delivery, while pending run plus reinjection need blocks new event recognition, each returning a busy indication. Each deliverable event is left for host handling when L1 did not request interception or converted to a simple nested exit with matching indication.

Nonmaskable and regular interrupt blocking share global flag gating and shadow masking with different guest bypass rules. Nonmaskable delivery is blocked when the global flag is clear; in guest mode with L1 requesting such exits it is never blocked, otherwise virtualized state or software mask plus shadow decides. Regular interrupt evaluation in guest mode samples enable from L1 saved flags when L1 uses virtual masking else from current flags, bypasses shadow when L1 requests interrupt exits, while host mode uses encrypted aware sampling; shadow otherwise blocks.

Virtualized nonmaskable enablement and global flag sampling choose backing storage by mode. Virtual nonmaskable state applies only when a global toggle allows it and execution is outside guest mode, using the primary control interrupt field; guest mode disables it. Global flag sampling prefers virtualized control storage when present, otherwise per vCPU software state. L1 interest in nonmaskable exits on SVM comes from the cached intercept bitmap.

On the VMX nesting path, L1 interest in nonmaskable exits derives from pin based execution controls of the cached outer control structure, true exactly when the nonmaskable exiting control is set. This contrasts with the SVM path which consults an intercept bitmap.
